mcqs.question: Which comparison correctly describes colloids in relation to solutions and suspensions?

options.A: Colloids have particle size larger than 1000 nm and settle out on standing, like suspensions.
options.B: Colloids have particle size between 1 nm and 1000 nm, do not settle, and exhibit the Tyndall effect, unlike solutions where particles are <1 nm.
options.C: Colloids are homogeneous mixtures where particles are molecularly dissolved, similar to solutions.
options.D: Colloids are heterogeneous mixtures with visible particles, similar to suspensions.

mcqs.answer: Colloids have particle size between 1 nm and 1000 nm, do not settle, and exhibit the Tyndall effect, unlike solutions where particles are <1 nm.
mcqs.explanation: Colloids contain particles in the size range 1–1000 nm. They remain dispersed and do not settle under gravity, but they scatter light (Tyndall effect). Solutions have particles <1 nm and are completely transparent, while suspensions have particles >1000 nm that settle out. Hence option B correctly captures these distinctions.

mcqs.learning_point: Compare particle size and visibility in different mixtures
mcqs.question: In a competitive‑exam style question, a student must match each type of mixture with its typical particle‑size range and visibility. Which of the following matches is correct?

options.A: Solution – particle size 0.1–1 nm, invisible to the naked eye.
options.B: Suspension – particle size 1–100 nm, visible as a faint haze.
options.C: Colloid – particle size >1000 nm, settles on standing.
options.D: Suspension – particle size 1–1000 µm, visible as distinct particles.

mcqs.answer: Solution – particle size 0.1–1 nm, invisible to the naked eye.
mcqs.explanation: In solutions the solute particles are molecular or ionic, typically <1 nm, making the mixture completely transparent. Suspensions contain particles >1000 nm (often µm range) that settle and are easily seen. Colloids have intermediate particle sizes (1–1000 nm) and show the Tyndall effect but do not settle. Therefore only option A correctly describes a solution.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a mixture in the context of matter?

options.A: A pure substance composed of only one type of particle.
options.B: A combination of two or more substances in which each retains its own chemical identity.
options.C: A substance formed by chemical bonding of elements.
options.D: A homogeneous solution where solute particles are chemically combined with solvent.

mcqs.answer: A combination of two or more substances in which each retains its own chemical identity.
mcqs.explanation: A mixture is formed when two or more substances are physically combined; no chemical reaction occurs, so each component keeps its original properties. Option B captures this definition, whereas the other options describe pure substances, compounds, or solutions where a chemical interaction is implied.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a homogeneous mixture from a heterogeneous mixture?

options.A: In a homogeneous mixture, the components are uniformly distributed and cannot be seen separately, whereas in a heterogeneous mixture, the components are unevenly distributed and can be seen as distinct phases.
options.B: Homogeneous mixtures always consist of gases, while heterogeneous mixtures consist only of solids.
options.C: Heterogeneous mixtures have particles smaller than 1 nm, homogeneous mixtures have larger particles.
options.D: Homogeneous mixtures settle on standing, heterogeneous mixtures do not.

mcqs.answer: In a homogeneous mixture, the components are uniformly distributed and cannot be seen separately, whereas in a heterogeneous mixture, the components are unevenly distributed and can be seen as distinct phases.
mcqs.explanation: Homogeneous mixtures (solutions, colloids) appear uniform throughout; individual components cannot be distinguished visually. Heterogeneous mixtures (suspensions, sand‑water) show visible separation of phases or particles. Options B, C, and D are incorrect generalisations.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a solution?

options.B: Sand mixed with water – a suspension.
options.C: Sugar dissolved in water – a solution.

mcqs.answer: Sugar dissolved in water – a solution.
mcqs.explanation: In a solution, the solute (sugar) particles are molecularly dispersed in the solvent (water) and are invisible, giving a clear mixture. Milk and fog are colloids, and sand‑water is a suspension, so only option C fits the definition of a solution.

mcqs.question: A mixture in which solid particles settle down on standing and are visible to the naked eye is called a:
mcqs.explanation: Suspensions contain relatively large solid particles (typically >1000 nm) that do not dissolve and eventually settle under gravity, making them visible. Solutions are clear, colloids remain dispersed, and alloys are solid mixtures of metals, so option C is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following mixtures is a colloid?

options.A: Salt dissolved in water – a solution.
options.B: Muddy water after standing – a suspension.
options.D: Air – a homogeneous mixture of gases.

mcqs.explanation: Milk contains fat globules and protein particles in the size range 1–1000 nm, which remain dispersed and scatter light (Tyndall effect), characteristic of colloids. Salt solution and air are true solutions, while muddy water is a suspension.

mcqs.learning_point: Compare particle size and visibility in different mixtures
mcqs.question: A student observes three mixtures: (i) sugar dissolved in water, (ii) muddy water that clears after a few minutes, (iii) milk. Which statement correctly compares the particle size and visibility among these mixtures?

options.A: In (i) particles are molecular size and invisible; in (ii) particles are large and settle, visible; in (iii) particles are intermediate size, cause Tyndall effect, and do not settle.
options.B: In (i) particles are large and settle; in (ii) particles are molecular size; in (iii) particles are invisible.
options.C: All three have particles larger than 1000 nm and are visible.
options.D: Only (ii) shows the Tyndall effect; (i) and (iii) do not.

mcqs.answer: In (i) particles are molecular size and invisible; in (ii) particles are large and settle, visible; in (iii) particles are intermediate size, cause Tyndall effect, and do not settle.
mcqs.explanation: Sugar solution contains dissolved ions/molecules (<1 nm) – invisible. Muddy water is a suspension with large particles (>1000 nm) that settle, making it visible. Milk is a colloid with particles 1–1000 nm; they stay dispersed, scatter light (Tyndall effect), and do not settle. Option A accurately reflects these characteristics.
